ledger.note: 567: 'On the death of Charibert in 567, Chilperic's estates were augmented when the brothers divided Charibert's kingdom among themselves and agreed to share Paris and the territory around it' (Chilperic I page). No page names the cities Chilperic received: Beauvais and Rouen are drawn because the Chlothar II page has the 599 Dormelles treaty reduce Chlothar II's kingdom 'to the regions of Beauvais, Amiens and Rouen' (so Neustria held them before 599) and the Charibert I page lists Rouen among Charibert's chief cities and gives Charibert 'Neustria (the region between the Somme and the Loire)'. Confidence 1: bridge. Charibert's Paris kingdom (561-567) has no dossier ('Kingdom of Paris' redirects to History of Paris), so the counterpart is the Frankish realm. The rest of Charibert's Neustria, the Seine-Loire land, is not placed here: the Chlothar II page has Guntram holding it.

region.text: Vannes, for which Waroch II did homage

ledger.note: 578: 'In 578, the Frankish king Chilperic I sent an army to fight Waroch along the Vilaine'; after three days Waroch 'did homage for Vannes, sent his son as a hostage, and agreed to pay an annual tribute' (Waroch II page; the Chilperic I page calls Chilperic's dominion over the Bretons 'relatively secure'). The counterpart is Waroch's Vannetais (Bro Waroch, Gwened, now Morbihan; the Bro Waroch page dates it 'from around AD 490 to around 635'), which was alive in 578; breton-kingdoms (eu-06) starts only in 587, the year 'Guntram compelled obedience from Waroch'. Bro Waroch has no dossier yet (listed under counterparts_needing_dossiers). Reviewer finding applied.

584: Chilperic I is murdered. The Waroch II page says only that Waroch 'subsequently broke his oath' (undated) and that 'in 587, Guntram compelled obedience from Waroch'; the relation to Neustria is therefore closed at Chilperic's death on a bridge (confidence 1). Counterpart changed from breton-kingdoms to Bro Waroch, which was alive in 578-584 (reviewer finding).

region.text: Tours and Poitiers, won over to Austrasia by Brunhilda's envoys and recovered by Guntram

ledger.note: 584: After Chilperic's death 'Two envoys from Brunhilde ... succeeded in swaying Limoges, Tours, and Poitiers'; Guntram's troops recovered them and they returned to Guntram and Clothar (undated on the page). Guntram ceded Tours to Austrasia at Andelot in 587. The Chlothar II page also says Ansoald was 'responsible for regaining control of cities Neustria had lost since the death of Chilperic' (names no city; the Fredegund page names no territory lost or regained after 584), so the loss stays at confidence 1.

587: 'In 587, he [Guntram] managed to capture the towns of Angers, Saintes, and Nantes' (Chlothar II page). The page does not say from whom the towns were taken. Only Saintes is placed in Neustria, by the Chilperic I page (Chilperic's 575 gain 'places in Aquitaine such as Saintes'); Angers and Nantes are not booked as Neustrian losses because no page says Neustria held them. Reviewer finding applied (the Seine-Loire land no longer enters Neustria).

596: 'In 596, Clotaire and Fredegund took Paris, which was supposed to be held in common.' The brothers' kingdoms shared Paris from 567; the counterpart is the Frankish realm whose other kingdoms held it in common.

599: Theuderic II and Theudebert II defeat Chlothar II at Dormelles, 'forcing him to sign a treaty that reduced his kingdom to the regions of Beauvais, Amiens and Rouen'; the rest was split between the two brothers. Paris (taken in 596) lies outside those regions, so it is lost; the page does not say to which brother (Theuderic II read, as frankish-burgundy's 600 gain draws the land around Paris). The former 599 loss of the Seine-Loire land is removed: no page has Neustria holding it (reviewer finding).

notes: Written for eu-07-x from five pages (Neustria, Francia, Chilperic I, Chlothar II, Austrasia); repaired 2026-10-25 after the reviewer's fail, with Chlodomer, Charibert I, Waroch II, Bro Waroch and Fredegund opened and Chlothar II re-read. The slug kingdom-of-neustria belongs to eu-07-c's dossier (717-724, Cliopatria's Kingdom of Neustria row), which that dossier says needs a Merovingian counterpart; this is that counterpart and a different slug on purpose. It is the same Frankish sub-kingdom and should share kingdom-of-neustria's colour. Scope: 511-613 only, ending when Chlothar II reunites the realm; the Neustria page's later dated events (Clovis II 639, Ebroin and Tertry 678-687, Ragenfrid 715-718) are carried by frankish-burgundy (639-660), kingdom-of-the-franks and kingdom-of-neustria. Overlap with kingdom-of-the-franks: its shape includes Neustria in 511-613 (it subtracts only Burgundy and, 612-613, Austrasia); the compiler must subtract this dossier's land too. REPAIR (reviewer finding, applied): the land between the Seine and the Loire is no longer Neustrian. The Chlothar II page says Guntram 'attempted to ... keep Neustrian lands he held between the Loire and Seine'; that is Guntram (Burgundy) holding the land, not Neustria. It is removed from the 584 gain, the 584-598 keyframes and the 599 loss; the Dormelles loss is now Paris (taken 596) and the northern cities. Angers and Nantes are no longer booked as Neustrian before 587; only Saintes (Chilperic's 575 gain) is lost in 587. Beauvais and Rouen (Oise, Seine-Maritime) enter at 567 at confidence 1: the Chlothar II page has the 599 treaty reduce the kingdom 'to the regions of Beauvais, Amiens and Rouen', so Neustria held them before 599; the Chilperic I page says only that his estates were 'augmented' in 567 when Charibert's kingdom was divided, and the Charibert I page names no shares (it lists Rouen among Charibert's chief cities and gives Charibert 'Neustria (the region between the Somme and the Loire)'). Added 524: Chlothar I's Touraine and Poitou (Chlodomer page). Still not on the pages: Chlothar I's other 511-557 growth (Burgundy 534, Provence 536, Paris 558), Sigebert's seizure of Soissons, the 575 Auvergne land, Austrasia's share of the 599 remainder (confidence 1; the matching gain is in kingdom-of-austrasia), which of Charibert's cities Chilperic took in 567 (the Fredegund page is silent too). Breton tie: the 578-584 vassal pair now names bro-waroch (Waroch II's Vannetais, alive in 578; Bro Waroch page: c. 490-c. 635), which has no dossier yet; breton-kingdoms (eu-06) starts in 587. The date of Waroch's broken oath is not on the pages (584 used, confidence 1). The Chilperic I page is inconsistent on the year of his death (infobox and body September 584, lead 583); 584 is used. Charibert's Paris kingdom (561-567) and Chlodomer's Orléans kingdom (511-524) have no articles and no dossiers, so their counterpart is kingdom-of-the-franks. Chlothar II page: Reims was assigned to Neustria in 623 and returned in 626 (not drawn). Overlap with frankish-burgundy: its 595 gain (Toulouse, Agen, Nantes) and 600 gain (Seine-Loire land) are no longer mirrored by Neustrian losses; the 599 Paris loss is the only Neustrian loss to Theuderic II's realm. Gazetteer names needed: places Saintes, Cambrai, Tournai, Boulogne-sur-Mer, Thérouanne, Beauvais, Vannes; region Neustria. Saintes is drawn with a lon/lat radius.
